question: A quality lead wants Claude to stop producing figures that do not appear anywhere in the reports uploaded to a project. Which addition to the project instructions best supports this?
options: A) Tell Claude to add a disclaimer to every answer noting that figures may not have been verified.
B) Tell Claude to answer only from the uploaded reports and to say plainly when a figure is not in them.
C) Tell Claude to always give a numeric answer, choosing the closest available figure when none matches.
D) Tell Claude that accuracy is extremely important and that mistakes are unacceptable in this project.
correct_answers: B) Tell Claude to answer only from the uploaded reports and to say plainly when a figure is not in them.
explanations: A blanket disclaimer shifts responsibility to the reader instead of preventing the problem.
Correct. This scopes the source and gives an explicit alternative to inventing a number.
This actively instructs the behaviour the quality lead is trying to prevent.
Emphasis without a rule gives no actionable behaviour to follow when a figure is missing.
